description: Install and configure Playwright for E2E testing. Set up the test infrastructure so subsequent features can write and run tests.
steps: Run `npm install -D @playwright/test` to add Playwright as a dev dependency
Run `npx playwright install chromium` to download the Chromium browser binary

Create `playwright.config.ts` at the project root with: baseURL 'http://localhost:3000', webServer config to run `npm run dev` (auto-start before tests, wait for port 3000, reuseExistingServer true, set env CLIENT_ID=arsh-sandhu), single project 'chromium', output folder 'playwright-report/', testDir 'tests/e2e', set use.actionTimeout to 10000, timeout per test to 30000
Create a minimal smoke test file `tests/e2e/smoke.spec.ts` that just navigates to '/' and asserts the page title or brand name is visible - this validates the infrastructure works
Run `npm run test:e2e` to confirm the smoke test passes with the dev server auto-starting
acceptance_criteria: `npm run test:e2e` script exists and runs Playwright
playwright.config.ts exists with correct baseURL, webServer, chromium project, and output settings
The smoke test passes (page loads and brand name is visible)
`npm run build` still succeeds with no TS errors from the new config file
verification: Run `npm run test:e2e` and confirm all tests pass
Run `npm run build` and confirm no TypeScript errors
findings: 1. Chromium requires system libraries (libnspr4, libnss3, etc.) that are not pre-installed on this Amazon Linux sandbox. Had to install via dnf + manual rpm extraction for nss (read-only /etc/pki blocked normal install). 2. The Supabase client throws if NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are not set, even on the landing page. Added dummy placeholder values in webServer env to prevent crashes. 3. Brand name 'SHREDCODE' appears multiple times on the landing page, so the smoke test uses .first() to avoid strict mode violations.
